question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $9,$ the additive inverse of $-5$ modulo $9$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-5$ modulo $9$ is the integer $0\le x<9$ such that

$$
x+(-5)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$

Notice that $5+(-5)≡0,$ so $x≡5\,(\text{mod}\,9),$ which is already in the required form. 

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-5$ modulo $9$ is $5.$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
